cur:catacombs2-girona-sant-feliu-frieze-.summary: Seven scenes run in a single line across this frieze, set high in the presbytery wall. Soldiers lead Peter away under arrest; Christ heals the paralytic, changes water into wine beside three jars at Cana, and, at the centre, stretches his hands over two baskets of bread held by apostles, with more baskets at their feet. To the right he opens a blind man's eyes and foretells Peter's denial over the cockerel, and at the end Peter strikes water from the rock for kneeling soldiers to drink.
facts: It repeats seven of the eight scenes of the neighbouring 'sarcophagus of Saint Felix' in a different order, suggesting the same workshop or model.
Catalan Wikipedia notes that some scholars regard it as a local copy of a model from Rome rather than a Roman import.

cur:manuscripts2-otto-iii-crucifixion-en.summary: Above, Christ in a long robe hangs on a golden cross between the two thieves, with the Virgin and John, the lance-bearer and the sponge-bearer, sun and moon, and soldiers dividing his garment below. In the lower register his body is taken down from the cross and laid in a sarcophagus by Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus. The page sets the death and burial of Christ side by side.
facts: The Gospels of Otto III has 276 leaves, twelve canon tables, a double-page portrait of the emperor, four evangelist portraits and 29 full-page miniatures of New Testament scenes; it was produced at Reichenau around 1000.
The Bayerische Staatsbibliothek has published the whole manuscript online with a Public Domain Mark, so every page can be studied in detail.

cur:objects-kells-market-cross.summary: The centre of the cross-head on the west face shows the Crucifixion, flanked on the arms by scenes from the lives of St Peter and of the desert fathers Paul and Anthony, including the Denial of Peter. Christ is set at the meeting point of the arms, the axis on which all the other stories turn. The cross once stood at the abbey's eastern gate, marking the threshold of the monastic town.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the 9th-century Market Cross originally stood at the abbey's eastern gate; legend says it was damaged by Cromwellian soldiers and used for hangings after the 1798 rebellion.
An inscription on its west face records its re-erection in 1688 (photographer's documentation).

Q570188.summary: Three angels sit around a table bearing a single chalice — the visitors who came to Abraham at Mamre, painted as an image of the Holy Trinity. In the traditional reading the central angel, in the deep red and blue robes of Christ, is the Son, inclining toward the Father as the circle of heads, wings and gestures draws the viewer into their silent communion around the eucharistic cup. It is perhaps the most celebrated of all Russian icons.
facts: It is traditionally held to have been painted in honour of Saint Sergius of Radonezh for the Trinity Lavra he founded.
Scholars debate which angel represents which Person of the Trinity; many identify the central angel with Christ, others with the Father.

After nearly a century in the Tretyakov Gallery (from 1929), the icon was handed to the Russian Orthodox Church in 2023 and shown first in Moscow's Cathedral of Christ the Saviour; since June 2024 it has stood in the iconostasis of the Lavra's Trinity Cathedral, despite conservators' warnings about its fragility.
